summary: Pair backend-scoped aggregate renderer counters with stable asset, node, primitive and resource identities without misreporting counters as GPU memory bytes, time or exact per-object cost.
objective: A runtime inventory states what the renderer counted, over which frame/pass scope, and which source nodes and shared resources were present, while attribution uncertainty remains visible.
applies_when: A loaded scene needs inspectable draw/resource provenance before a separately authorized performance investigation or cleanup check.
intent_signals: which glTF node contributes draw calls
renderer info is not GPU bytes
trace active texture to source asset
multi-pass counts reset at wrong time
example_prompts: Build a diagnostic inventory that relates WebGLRenderer.info totals to loaded glTF node and resource IDs.
Explain why hiding one object does not prove its exact GPU time or memory cost.
negative_signals: subtract totals to assign exact object cost
not_for: Running a benchmark or setting a universal performance budget.
Claiming WebGLRenderer counters describe WebGPU or every renderer backend.

principles: Name the backend, renderer revision, frame and pass/reset scope before interpreting counters. A number without its counting window is not comparable.
WebGLRenderer.info exposes aggregate render counters and active resource-object counts. They are not GPU byte allocation, GPU duration, CPU frame time or automatic per-object attribution.

Source provenance is a separate inventory: asset revision, stable exported node key, loaded Object3D, glTF mesh/primitive and referenced geometry, material and textures. Shared resources remain shared rather than charged repeatedly.
Visibility toggles or isolated passes can provide controlled deltas, but caching, culling, instancing, batching, shadows, postprocessing and shared resources limit causal attribution.
implementation: At load, build an application-side map from asset revision and exported stable keys to loaded nodes, primitives, geometries, materials and textures. Preserve source names only as readable labels, not unique identity.

For WebGLRenderer, capture renderer.info render calls, triangles, lines and points plus active geometry, texture and program inventory under a declared autoReset/reset policy. Record whether shadows, depth prepasses, postprocessing or multiple render calls are included.

Show selected node facts from geometry attributes/index, material slots, visibility, layers, instancing and shared-resource reference counts. Label theoretical primitive counts separately from renderer-observed frame totals.

If later diagnosis is authorized, compare controlled variants one at a time and report aggregate deltas as observations under that setup, not intrinsic per-object cost. Use timing or GPU-memory tools only through their separately documented interfaces.
On unload, release application-owned resources according to the disposal contract and observe inventory stabilization only as supporting evidence; counter changes alone do not prove absence of leaks.
observable_checks: Render one declared WebGL frame/pass configuration and record the reset boundary; totals from an added shadow or postprocess pass are not mislabeled as one beauty pass.
Select two nodes sharing one geometry or texture; the provenance panel shows both references while the shared resource appears once in the unique-resource inventory.
Hide or isolate one node and explain any aggregate delta with culling, instancing, batching and extra passes considered; no exact GPU-time or byte claim is derived from renderer.info.
Unload and reload the asset under the same setup; stable node keys resolve consistently and unresolved or duplicated keys are reported before interpreting resource counts.

creative_affordances: Use a source tree, resource-reference graph or selected-node delta panel according to the debugging question.
Highlight shared resources and extra passes visually without turning them into mandatory optimization targets.
known_limits: No performance, memory-pressure, GPU timing or benchmark check was run or authorized.
The cited renderer.info contract is WebGLRenderer-specific at the pinned Three.js revision; other backends require separate verified instrumentation.
Aggregate deltas do not establish exact per-object cost or causality.

claims.statement: At Three.js commit 4457aa3c5de4a05bbae4e0bee2d99d994c38a2bb, WebGLRenderer.info documents per-frame render counts for calls, triangles, points and lines, counts of active geometries and textures, a programs array, and configurable autoReset/reset handling for multiple render passes.
claims.scope: Pinned WebGLRenderer aggregate statistics; the fields do not document GPU bytes, GPU or CPU time, or exact per-object attribution.
